_note: level is an a-priori rating from the rubric and the size facts of each item (units, reference lines, hidden cases, features). It was assigned after the first baseline runs had started, and I had seen that almost every run passed, so it is NOT independent of those results; it is a hypothesis to test with weaker models and with no plan. Measured numbers come from eval/report.py, never from this file.

rubric.1: Pure integer functions. No heap, no text, no Result. One idea per function. A solver fails only on integer edge cases (overflow, negatives, zero).
rubric.2: Bytes in, Result or owned buffer out, one algorithmic idea, a strict contract (what is invalid is part of the task). Up to ~110 reference lines.
rubric.3: Several interacting units, or state in slices, or UTF-8 / lists / DP, or two directions that must agree. ~60-150 reference lines.
rubric.4: A grammar or rule system with several interacting phases and many edge rules (ranges, quoting, precedence, sections). 130+ reference lines, 6+ units, hundreds of hidden cases.
rubric.5: More than one module, effects (storage, network, clock) or an external contract, acceptance that needs a running service. Not a single plan of pure functions: it needs a breakdown first. (09-12 services; `bank`.)
